title: WPSS/679/2013 of Smt Champa Joshi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.679 of 2013
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. Alok Dalakoti, Advocate for the
petitioner and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
The contention of the petitioner is that she
was a candidate for appointment on the post of
Aganwadi Karyakarti for a particular ward in
District Almora. Though, she was at the top of the
select list, the appointment has not been made as
she was not permanently residing in a particular
Mohalla / ward. The petitioner moved a
representation before the District Magistrate,
Almora, which has been rejected vide order dated
04.05.2011 on the ground that she does not belong
to Vivekanandpuri ward, Almora. Thereafter, the
petitioner went to the Lokayukta where she did not
get any relief.
The petitioner submits that on a wrong
advice, she went to the Lokayukta, due to which
there is a delay in approaching this Court. The
appointment of Anganwadi Karyakarti is governed
by the Government Order dated 24.02.2009
wherein an appellate committee has also been
constituted to sort out the grievances regarding the
appointments of Aganwadi Karyakarti.
In view of the above, the writ petition is
disposed of directing the petitioner to move a
representation before the appellate committee. In
case, the petitioner moves a representation before
the appellate committee, which has been
constituted vide Government Order dated
24.02.2009, the same shall be disposed of in
accordance with law after hearing the petitioner
and respondent no.5. It is made clear that while
condoning the delay, the appellate committee shall
also consider the fact that the petitioner on a wrong
advice went to the Lokayukta for her grievances.
No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated 17.06.2013
Rawat

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. H. S. Dhillon, Advocate for the

superannuation on 31.07.2010 and he retired from

WPSS No.112 of 2006
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. H. C. Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioner and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing
Counsel for the respondents.
The petitioner has done his High School
Examination in the year 1982 from the Public
Inter-College, Doiwala, Dehradun, but the date of
birth of the petitioner has wrongly been shown as
26.02.1965 instead of 26.10.1965 in the High
School certificate.
In this regard, the petitioner submitted an
application dated 07.05.1984 (Annexure-5 to the
writ petition) before the Secretary, Madhyamik
Shiksha Parishad, U.P., Allahabad through the
District Inspector of School, Dehradun. The said
application of the petitioner is pending
consideration before the authority concerned.
The only ground taken in the counter
affidavit is that such a request can only be
accepted, if the same is made within two years
from the date of issuance of the certificate. The
certificate in question was issued on 24.06.1982
and the petitioner's application for correction of
his date of birth is dated 07.05.1984, which is
absolutely well within the stipulated period of two
years. The Principal, Government Inter College,
Rani Pokhari, Dehradun (from where the petitioner
passed Class-VI) had also gave an endorsement on
the application of the petitioner on 16.07.1984.
In the light of aforesaid, the writ petition is
disposed of directing the Secretary Board of High
School and Intermediate Education, U.P. /
respondent no.2 to decide the application for the
petitioner within three months from the date of
production of a certified copy of this order.
No order as to costs.

WPSS No.1985 of 2011
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. Vishal Singh Mahra, Advocate
for the petitioners and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya,
Standing Counsel for the State.
 The petitioners have been working on
contractual basis in the medical college prior to the
provincialization of the Dr. Sushila Tiwari
Memorial Forest Hospital (hereinafter referred
to as the "medical college"). The grievance of the
petitioners is that there is a clear provision in
clause 8 of the Resolution dated 04.02.2010
(Annexure-2 to the writ petition) that the service
conditions of contractual employees shall remain
same as it was earlier. The petitioners now contend
that after provincialization of the medical college,
they are being deprived of various facilities such as
Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, Hill
Allowance, etc., but prior to its provincialization
they would being given such facilities.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that the present matter is squarely covered by the
decision of this Court passed in Writ Petition
No.408 of 2012 (S/S) titled as "Puran Chandra
Tiwari & others Vs. State of Uttarakhand &
another vide judgment dated 21.05.2013. The
learned Standing Counsel also concedes this fact.
Consequently, the present writ petition is
allowed in terms of the aforesaid WPSS
No.408/2013. A mandamus is issued to the
respondent authorities directing them to give all
benefits, which the petitioners were getting prior to
its provincialization.
No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)

WPSS No.477 of 2009 pdf
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. Nagesh Agarwal, Advocate for
the petitioner and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya,
Standing Counsel for the State.
The petitioner was a candidate for the
selection to the post of Primary Teacher (Urdu)
and he appeared in the selection process.
The only prayer of the petitioner is that his
answer script be sent for re-evaluation or
reexamination by a fresh selection committee /
examiner.
The State Government has filed a counter
affidavit stating that there is no provision for re-examination of the answersheet and that the
scrutiny of the same can only be done, in fact,
there is no prayer for the scrutiny in the present
writ petition.
After hearing the learned counsel for the
parties, the Court is of the opinion that the re-examination of the answersheet cannot be done as
it is not permissible under the law.
Consequently, the writ petition has no merit
and is hereby dismissed accordingly. No order as
to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. K. N. Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioners and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing
Counsel for the State.
The contention of the petitioners is that they
were working as "Shiksha Acharya" and now
under the Government Orders, they are liable to be
made "Shiksha Mitra". Earlier, a writ petition
No.261/2011 (S/S) was filed by the petitioners,
which was disposed of vide order dated
22.11.2011 directing the educational authority to
decide the representation of the petitioners.
Thereafter, the educational authority rejected the
representation of the petitioners on the ground that
the petitioners were working as Shiksha Acharya
in an Education Guarantee Centre, which never
had an approval from the educational authority.
The Addl. District Education Officer
(Basic), Champawat has filed its counter affidavit
stating that neither the educational authority has
given their approval for running of such centres
nor any approval was accorded for appointment of
the petitioners as Shiksha Acharya and that the
petitioners never rendered their services as Shiksha
Acharya in a centre, which is recognized by the
authority. Although, as per the contention of
learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioners
were selected for Shiksha Acharya and sent for
training for a period of 20 days, but there is
nothing on record that the petitioners were
teaching in a centre, which is recognized /
approved by the State authorities. The centre
where the petitioners were teaching was not in the
approved list prepared by the State authorities.
Considering the above facts and
circumstances of the case, the writ petition is liable
to be dismissed and is dismissed accordingly.
No order as to costs.

WPSS No.1427 of 2011
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for the
petitioner and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing
Counsel for the State.
The petitioner is the son of late Shri Dev
Singh Panwar, who died while in service of the
Cooperative Society, Uttarkashi. From the record
available before this Court, it appears that the
petitioner only attained his majority in the year
2006-2007, however, he could not claim
appointment on compassionate grounds as his
father was still not being treated as a "Government
employee" and, although a writ petition was
pending before this Court, which was ultimately
allowed vide order dated 31.03.2006 passed in
WPSS No.4796/2001.
However, the claim of the petitioner for
appointment on compassionate ground has been
rejected by the department on two grounds i.e. the
petitioner's father was not in a regular employment
and, secondly, the petitioner's application for
appointment on compassionate ground was highly
belated. This Court is of the considered opinion
that the stand taken by the department is not
correct in view of the subsequent developments i.e.
the Secretary vide order 01.11.2012 (Annexure-2
to the rejoinder affidavit) has treated the
petitioner's father as "Government employee" and,
subsequently similarly situated employees, whose
father or mother as the case may be died in
harness, have been given appointment on
compassionate grounds (in fact, one example is of
the year 2012).
Considering the above facts and
circumstances of the case, the writ petition is
disposed of directing the respondent authority to
reconsider the appointment of the petitioner on
compassionate ground in the light of the aforesaid
two developments. Needful be done within a
period of eight weeks from the date of production
of a certified copy of this order. No order as to
costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated 21.05.2013

WPMS No.1036 of 2013 pdf
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Mr. Manish Arora, Advocate present for the
petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional Chief
Standing Counsel present for the State of
Uttarakhand.
The petitioner is a member of the
Cooperative Society. He challenges the action of
the State authorities, who are now conducting
elections for the post of Director of Zila Bheshaj
Sahkari Sangh and the objections regarding the
same has not been looked into.
Be that as may, the grievance of the
petitioner cannot be considered as admittedly the
date of the election for the post of Director has
already been notified on 06.02.2012. In view of the
law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in
Mohinder Singh Gill & another Vs. The Chief
Election Commissioner, New Delhi & others
1978 (1) SCC 485 and N. P. Ponnuswami Vs.
The Returning Officer, Namakkal
Constituency, Namakkal, Salem Dist. & others
1952 AIR SC 64 wherein it was held that if the
schedule of an election is notified, no interference
should be normally made, the present writ petition
fails and is dismissed accordingly.
No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. D. S. Mehta, Advocate for the
petitioner and Mr. B. D. Upadhyaya, Advocate for
the Uttarakhand Power Corporation.
 The petitioner did not pay his electricity
dues. The Uttarakhand Power Corporation made a
demand from the petitioner to pay the electricity
dues. Against the demand letter, the petitioner
filed a complaint before the District Consumer
Forum, which was dismissed vide order dated
15.12.2001. Feeling aggrieved by the order dated
15.12.2001, he filed an appeal before the State
Consumer Forum, which was disposed of directing
the Corporation to prepare fresh bills, excluding
the charges of a particular period, though, a facility
was granted to the petitioner to pay dues through
easy installments.
 Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner filed a
revision before the National Consumer
Commission, whereby the order of the State
Consumer Forum dated 08.09.2004 was set aside
and the complaint of the petitioner was dismissed.
Eventually, the petitioner filed a Special Leave
Petition before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which
was also dismissed.
Thereafter, the Uttarakhand Power
Corporation has issued a recovery proceeding
dated 16.12.2008, which has been challenged in
the present writ petition.
Considering the above facts of the case, the
Court of the considered view that the writ petition
has no merit since he has already lost his case upto
the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The writ petition is dismissed accordingly.
No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated 16.05.2013

WPSS No.484 of 2006 pdf*
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Heard Mr. Harendra Belwal, Advocate for the
petitioner and Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing
Counsel present for the State.
All the present petitioners were appointed as
Assistant Teachers in Government School and what
is common to all of them is that the appointment in
each case was on compassionate grounds as their
father or mother, as the case may be, died in harness.
Now, the petitioners claim seniority and all other
consequential benefits. This Court is however
amazed as to how such appointments (i.e.
appointment on compassionate grounds) could be
made in the first place under the U.P. Recruitment of
Dependents of Government Servants Dying in
Harness Rules, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as the
Rules of 1974) in as much as on the face of it such
appointments are not permissible as they are to be
made only on the Ministerial post of Class III or
Class IV.
Be that as it may, no counter affidavit has
been filed by the State, therefore, the writ petition in
any case cannot be finally adjudicated as there is no
version of the State. Before this Court, it is the
contention of the petitioners that they filed several
representations, but all in vein. The last
representation dated 15.03.2006 is pending
consideration.
The writ petition is disposed of with the
direction that the answering authority shall first
record the reasons as to whether in the first place
such appointments (i.e. appointment on
compassionate grounds) are permissible under the
law and only thereafter decide the representation of
the petitioners by a reasoned and speaking order
within a period of eight weeks from the date of
production of a certified copy of this order. It is
made clear that in case the representation of the
petitioners is not on record, the petitioners are at
liberty to file it before the authority concerned
alongwith a certified copy of this order. No order as
to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated 13.05.2013
Rawat
